report.summary: Chunk 2 of canary.py defines closed vocabularies, constants, and nonce utilities. All claims about behaviour are checkable within the chunk.

handoff.purpose: Define closed vocabularies (CANARY_STATUSES, SEVERITIES, FAILING_STATUSES), constants, and nonce generation.

symbols.name: CANARY_STATUSES
symbols.note: Closed tuple of five status strings: ok, wrong_answer, timeout, unavailable, error.

symbols.name: FAILING_STATUSES
symbols.note: Frozenset: wrong_answer, timeout, error. Notably excludes 'unavailable'.

symbols.name: new_nonce
symbols.note: Returns a string like 'K7F3A9C1' using secrets.token_hex.

symbols.name: _rng
symbols.note: Returns a random.Random seeded deterministically from nonce string. Not exported.

claims.text: CLOSED -- nothing may invent a sixth, and in particular ``unavailable`` and ``wrong_answer`` are separate members because a report that merges them is a report that lies.
claims.why: CANARY_STATUSES is defined as a tuple with exactly five members, and the docstring explicitly warns against adding a sixth or merging unavailable and wrong_answer.

claims.text: Only ``liveness`` trips the exit code -- see the module docstring.
claims.why: The claim references the module docstring and exit code behaviour, which are not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``unavailable`` is deliberately absent: we never asked, so there is nothing to have failed.
claims.why: FAILING_STATUSES is a frozenset containing 'wrong_answer', 'timeout', 'error' but not 'unavailable', matching the claim.
The claim refers to the behaviour of the history file; this chunk only defines the path constant, not the file operations.

claims.text: This runs often; the 32b is not a health check, it is a bill.
claims.why: The comment is informal and references usage frequency and cost, which are not verifiable from the constant definition alone.

claims.text: same set as ``council.session.VENDOR_KEYS`` so ``--vendors`` means one thing repo-wide
claims.why: The claim references another module (council.session.VENDOR_KEYS) not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Enough to see what a lane actually said, not enough to turn history.jsonl into a transcript store.
claims.why: The claim refers to the effect of the constant on history storage, which is not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: Long enough to be a baseline, short enough that a lane which legitimately got faster stops being compared against last month.
claims.why: The claim references the comparison logic, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A lane counts as materially slower only if it is BOTH a large multiple of its median AND absolutely slow enough for a human to care. Either test alone cries wolf: a 0.2s -> 0.6s local hop is 3x and means nothing.
claims.why: The claim describes the combination logic of these two constants, which is not implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: Fresh PER PROBE PER LANE, not per run: a reused nonce cannot distinguish a lane that answered from a lane (or a cache, or a shared transcript) that echoed somebody else's answer -- which is the exact confusion the anchoring incident was made of.
claims.why: The claim describes usage context and rationale; the function itself only generates a nonce string. The guarantee of freshness per probe per lane is not enforced by this code alone.

claims.text: Deterministic per-nonce randomness, so ``build`` and ``check`` agree.
claims.why: The claim refers to build and check functions not present in this chunk.

observations.what: The docstring for CANARY_STATUSES explicitly forbids adding a sixth status or merging unavailable and wrong_answer, and the code defines exactly five.
FAILING_STATUSES excludes 'unavailable' as stated in its docstring.
VENDOR_KEYS docstring claims it matches council.session.VENDOR_KEYS, but that module is not in this chunk.

new_nonce generates a string starting with 'K' and 7 uppercase hex digits, but the docstring example shows 8 characters (K7F3A9C1). The code uses token_hex(4) which produces 8 hex digits, then takes [:7] resulting in 7 digits after 'K', total 8 characters. The example 'K7F3A9C1' is 8 characters, consistent.
